message.content:
{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Shared explicit contract facts and constraints (repeat of every explicit item):
- For PUT on an entry, a missing/omitted description field means: do not modify the existing description in storage.
- For PUT, a description value of null must clear the stored description to database NULL.
- For PUT, a description value of empty string ("") must be saved as the empty string in storage (not as NULL).
- The frontend "clear" user action MUST submit description: null.
- The description string maximum length is 255 characters; this constraint is continuously valid and must be enforced/observed.
- Do NOT automatically convert an omitted description to null. Do NOT fold empty string into null.
- Creation (POST) rules remain unchanged; do not alter create behavior here. (Frontend omission: do not change create flows; this prompt does not prescribe create behavior.)

Frontend implementation instructions (only actionable items; do not change unspecified server behavior):
1) Data model and intent tracking
   - Maintain, per edit session, a tri-state intent for the description field: {omitted, explicit-null, explicit-string}.
     - omitted: the user has not changed the description since loading the edit form.
     - explicit-null: the user invoked the UI "clear" action (or equivalent) and intends to clear to NULL.
     - explicit-string: the user has typed a value (possibly empty string "") and intends that exact string to be saved.
   - Do not infer intent from absence of user interaction; explicitly set the state when the user performs actions.

2) UI behaviors and mapping to request payload
   - When user opens edit form, initialize the intent to omitted.
   - If the user edits the description input (including deleting all characters and leaving the input empty) mark intent as explicit-string and set the value to "" (empty string) if the input is empty.
   - If the user activates the designated "clear" control, set intent to explicit-null and clear the visible input as appropriate; the key requirement is that the submitted payload must contain description: null.
   - When building the PUT JSON body to send to the server:
     - If intent === omitted: do NOT include the description property at all in the JSON object.
     - If intent === explicit-null: include "description": null in the JSON.
     - If intent === explicit-string: include "description": "..." with the exact string value (can be "" for empty string).
   - Ensure request uses the same HTTP method and endpoint already used for PUT; do not change create (POST) code or its payload rules.

3) Client-side validation and UX
   - Enforce max length 255 on the description input (visual count and programmatic prevention). Do not allow submission of a non-null string whose length > 255.
   - If a user attempts to submit a string >255, block the submission and show a clear validation error message. If backend returns a length-related error, display it to the user.
   - Explicit empty-string input is valid; allow saving an empty string. Do not convert empty-string to null in any UI logic.

4) Network/serialization notes
   - Send plain JSON for PUT. The presence vs absence of the description key is significant; ensure JSON serialization omits the key entirely for omitted intent.
   - For explicit-null send JSON: { ..., "description": null, ... }.
   - For explicit-string send JSON: { ..., "description": "" } or the typed string.

5) Acceptance test cases the frontend must implement/verify
   - Edit without touching description -> PUT payload does NOT contain description; server must leave description unchanged.
   - Click "clear" control -> PUT payload contains "description": null; server must set database description to NULL.
   - Delete all text in the input and save (no separate "clear" control) -> PUT payload contains "description": "" and server must store empty string.
   - Attempt to type >255 chars -> block submission with client-side validation; show error.

6) Side-specific omission statement
   - This frontend prompt does NOT define server-side storage, DB update logic, or POST/create behavior. It does not change creation rules; do not modify POST endpoints or their validation as part of this work.

Do not add or rely on any historical or unspecified behavior beyond the facts above. Implement only what is stated: preserve omission-as-no-change, null-as-clear-to-NULL, empty-string-as-empty-string, and frontend must submit null explicitly for the "clear" action while enforcing 255-char limit."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Shared explicit contract facts and constraints (repeat of every explicit item):
- For PUT on an entry, a missing/omitted description field in the request means: do not modify the existing description in storage.
- For PUT, a description value of null must clear the stored description to database NULL.
- For PUT, a description value of empty string ("") must be saved as the empty string in storage (not as NULL).
- The frontend "clear" action MUST submit description: null.
- The description string maximum length is 255 characters; this constraint is continuously valid and must be enforced/observed.
- Do NOT automatically convert an omitted description to null. Do NOT fold empty string into null.
- Creation (POST) rules remain unchanged; do not alter create behavior here. (Backend omission: do not change POST/create validation/semantics as part of this change.)

Backend implementation instructions (only actionable items; do not change unspecified client behavior):
1) Request parsing and presence detection
   - When handling PUT, detect whether the JSON payload includes the description key. Rely on the JSON parser or request deserializer to determine presence versus absence (do not assume absent keys are present with null).
   - Branch solely on key presence and value:
     - Key absent -> treat as omitted: do not touch the description column in the update.
     - Key present && value === null -> treat as explicit clear: set the description column to SQL NULL.
     - Key present && value is a string (including empty string "") -> treat as explicit-string and set the description column to that exact string.

2) Validation
   - If the request includes a non-null string for description, validate its length <= 255. If >255, reject the PUT with a 400 Bad Request and a clear validation error message indicating the 255-character limit.
   - If description is null or absent, length validation does not apply.

3) Database update semantics
   - Build the UPDATE statement (or ORM update object) dynamically so the description column is only included in the SET clause when the description key is present in the request.
     - Example approach (pseudocode):
       - updates = {}
       - if request.hasKey('description'):
           updates.description = request.value('description') // may be null or ""
       - if updates not empty: perform UPDATE entries SET <keys from updates> WHERE id = :id
       - if updates empty: do not include description in update and proceed with other fields or return no-op response per existing behavior
   - Do NOT use SQL constructs that collapse presence/value semantics (for example, do NOT use COALESCE(description_param, description_column) as that would conflate null/omitted semantics).
   - When setting description to NULL, bind a database NULL parameter so the column value becomes NULL.
   - When setting description to empty string, bind an empty string parameter so the column stores the empty string.

4) Responses and consistency
   - If the update succeeds, return the same success status and body shape currently used for PUT. If the request is a no-op (description omitted and no other changes), follow existing service semantics for no-op updates (do not invent a new response code).
   - If validation fails (length >255), return 400 with a descriptive message; do not accept or coerce the value.

5) Acceptance test cases the backend must implement/verify
   - PUT with no description key -> database description remains unchanged.
   - PUT with "description": null -> database description becomes SQL NULL.
   - PUT with "description": "" -> database description becomes empty string ("").
   - PUT with "description": string longer than 255 -> respond 400 and do not modify the entry.
   - Ensure empty string is not converted to NULL and omitted field is not converted to NULL.

6) Side-specific omission statement
   - This backend prompt does NOT mandate frontend UI behavior or how the client constructs requests beyond the contract above. It does not change creation (POST) endpoints or their validation rules; do not modify post/create semantics as part of this implementation.

Do not add or assume any historical or unspecified behavior beyond the facts above. Implement only the exact semantics: omit-as-no-change, null-as-clear-to-NULL, empty-string-as-empty-string, and enforce the 255-character string limit when a non-null string is provided."
  }
}
